doors.note: The cities directory as cached 2026-10-15 (124 KB): no cards of its own (the AI classifier files it as a link-aggregator), a link per city and per country. The crawl follows them under discoveryAllowedPatterns whereto.party/in/ (maxAdditionalUrls 60); 62 city/country pages are in the cache this week. Its flight data lists 54 rows of city stats, from which the page-data reader built 2 records in run 20261017-054812 ("The Magic of Tomorrowland" with no venue — a directory row, not a card).

The representative city page as cached 2026-10-17T18:45Z: 20 server-rendered cards — title (the flyer alt), "Tokyo · Venue", "Weekday, D Month YYYY · HH:MM – HH:MM", price, flyer, a link to the card's own /events/<slug> page. The flight data says more rows exist (offset 25) behind /api/events, which robots.txt disallows — the first page is the site's answer. The 20 Tokyo cards today are all 2026-10-17 (the page shows the coming week first).
Cached 2026-10-17. One wildcard group by design (the file says so).

recon.notes: Recheck 2026-10-17 from the page cache. Every /in/ page has the same shape; Tokyo is documented card by card. Run 20261017-054812: 62 pages, 398 rows, 25 kept, 234 AI-dropped — the cities are all inside the configured scope (the directory's own links); 42 of 267 rows carry city "unknown" because the page's city (Toulouse, Osaka, Kuala Lumpur, Lisbon, Taoyuan …) has no scraper-cities key, which is correct. Sixteen rows titled "Where to party in <City>" (the page's own h1, fused with the first card) and "Up next"/"Tomorrow" section labels are reader artefacts, not cards.

coverage.basis: The Tokyo page's 20 cards, every one. The other ~60 city pages are read by the same crawl and the same reader but are not enumerated here (homogeneous shape; aggregator records never win a field). publishedEventCount counts the documented page.

traps.label: "Where to party in Toulouse" (the page h1: eyebrow "Where to party in" + "Toulouse") read as an event with the first card's venue
traps.why: The city page's heading is not a card. Run 20261017-054812 carries 16 such rows (Toulouse, Port Adelaide, Belgium, Brussels, Paris, India, Kolkata, Lombok Utara, Hakuba, Osaka, Manila, Taguig, Porto, Spain, Madrid, Taoyuan), each dated like the page's first card — the flat splitter fused the heading with the card below it on one-card pages.

evidence.quote: Where to party in Toulouse | whereto.party

traps.label: "Up next", "Tomorrow", "Don't see your city?"
traps.why: Section labels and the submit prompt between the cards; the daily audit flagged "Tomorrow" and "Don't see your city?" as non-events on 2026-10-17 and an earlier run carried "Up next" as a title.

traps.label: /in/australia, /in/japan, /in/philippines … list the same cards as their cities
traps.why: The directory links countries beside cities; a country page is the union of its city pages (Australia = Sydney + Melbourne + Brisbane + …), so every card is read twice and folds in dedup.

expect.note: Read twice and deduplicated — correct behaviour.

openQuestions: 2026-10-01: each city page ships its first 20 rows as flight data (initialHasMore/initialNextOffset) and loads the rest from /api/events?offset=&limit=&city_id= (read off the page's own bundle); robots.txt says "Disallow: /api/", so the scraper reads the first page only (the site's answer). Sydney holds 38 rows, Melbourne/Tokyo/Bangkok also say more.
